instructions: The night before, or at least 4 hours ahead: Rinse the chana dal until the water runs clear. Put it in a bowl with 4 cups water and leave it on the counter.

Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, changing the water until it runs clear, then drain it. Put the rice in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave the lid on until the curry is ready.
Drain the dal. Peel the bottle gourd, cut out any seedy center, and cut it into 3/4-inch cubes. That should be about 3 cups.
Chop the onion, mince the garlic, and chop the tomatoes.
Heat 1 tsp of the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the dal, 1/4 tsp of the turmeric, 1/4 tsp of the chili powder and 1/2 tsp salt. Stir for 1 minute.
Add 3 cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes, until the dal is nearly tender.

Add the bottle gourd and cover. Cook for 10 minutes, until the dal and the gourd are both soft. Don't add water. The gourd gives off plenty. If the dal is still firm in the center, cook it for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tsp of the cumin seeds and the asafoetida. After about 20 seconds the seeds will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes, stirring often, until golden brown. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds.

Turn the heat to low. Stir in the remaining 1/2 tsp turmeric, the remaining 1/4 tsp chili powder, the coriander, the ground cumin, the garam masala and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, until they break down and oil shows at the edges.
Transfer the cooked dal and gourd, with their liquid, into the skillet. Stir gently and simmer for 5 minutes. If it is thicker than a stew, stir in up to 1/2 cup hot water.
Heat the remaining 2 tsp oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the remaining 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and stir for 20 seconds, until they sizzle. Pour it over the dal.
Stir in the cilantro and the kasuri methi crushed between your palms.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
advance_prep_notes: soak the chana dal at least 4 hours ahead or overnight
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (5 from 41) is the lead: chana dal and bottle gourd cooked soft together, a separate onion, tomato and spice masala, the two combined, then a cumin tempering with kasuri methi and cilantro to finish. Piping Pot Curry (4.89 from 26) agrees on the dal and gourd amounts and adds lime juice. The lead soaks the dal for 30 minutes and uses a pressure cooker, which the page times at over an hour in all; here the dal soaks ahead and cooks in a covered pot so the evening is 45 minutes. The lead's list forgets the tomatoes its method uses, and they are included. Ghee is swapped for oil to keep it vegan, the green chilies are left out to keep it mild, and the asafoetida is listed as gluten-free because some brands are cut with wheat flour.
